summary: The study investigates the effect of deposition temperature on the electrical properties and interface of high-k ZrO2 capacitors. The results show that the leakage current and dielectric constant are influenced by the deposition temperature, with the highest dielectric constant observed at 275°C due to the formation of tetragonal/cubic phases. The main leakage current mechanism is governed by the Poole–Frenkel conduction, and the interface quality is affected by oxygen inter-diffusion.
evidence: The electrical characteristics, i.e. leakage current and capacitance, of ZrO2 based metal–insulator–metal structures, grown at 225, 250 and 275◦C by atomic layer deposition, were studied. The lowest leakage current was obtained at 250◦C deposition temperature, while the highest dielectric constant (k ∼ 43) was measured for the samples grown at 275◦C, most probably due to the formation of tetragonal/cubic phases in the ZrO2 layer. We have shown that the main leakage current of these ZrO2 capacitors is governed by the Poole–Frenkel conduction mechanism. It was observed by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling that at 275◦C deposition temperature the oxygen content at and beyond the ZrO2/TiN interface is higher than at lower deposition temperatures, most probably due to oxygen inter-diffusion towards the electrode layer, forming a mixed TiN–TiOxNy interface layer. At and above 275◦C the ZrO2 layer changes its structure and becomes crystalline as proven by XRD analysis.
